preconditions.description: The number of intersections n is a positive integer between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and all(1 <= i <= n for i in range(1, n + 1)) and all(i <= a[i - 1] <= n for i in range(1, n + 1)) and all(a[i - 1] <= a[i] for i in range(1, n))
preconditions.description: The input array a has length n, where each a[i] (1-based) satisfies i ≤ a[i] ≤ n, and the sequence a is non-decreasing.

postconditions.description: The output is a space-separated string of n integers, where the i-th integer (1-based) is the minimum energy required to reach intersection i from intersection 1, computed as the minimum total energy over all possible paths from 1 to i.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= min_energies[i - 1] <= n for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: Each minimum energy value is a non-negative integer bounded by n.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition that enforces the correct computation of minimum energy for each intersection, including the use of shortcuts (1 unit of energy) when applicable (i.e., when moving from intersection i to a_i). The current expression does not capture the logic of shortcuts or the dynamic programming nature of the problem (e.g., min_energies[i] should be computed as the minimum of: 1) direct walk from 1 to i, 2) walk via shortcuts, 3) intermediate steps).
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Formally, for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n Mike is interested in finding minimum possible total energy of some sequence p_1 = 1, p_2, ..., p_k = i. ... if Mike chooses a sequence p_1 = 1, p_2, ..., p_k then for each 1 ≤ i < k satisfying p_i + 1 = a_{p_i} and a_{p_i} ≠ p_i Mike will spend only 1 unit of energy instead of |p_i - p_{i+1}|.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition that enforces the correct handling of shortcuts in the computation. Specifically, the minimum energy to reach intersection i must account for paths that use shortcuts (e.g., 1 -> a_1 -> ... -> i) where each shortcut contributes exactly 1 unit of energy.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: if Mike chooses a sequence p_1 = 1, p_2 = a_{p_1}, p_3 = a_{p_2}, ..., p_k = a_{p_{k-1}} - 1, he spends exactly k - 1 units of total energy walking around them.
